guide.name: Route 66 from Chicago to Santa Monica
guide.description: Nine days on the old Mother Road across eight states, with diners, neon motels, roadside giants and Route 66 museums from the Begin sign in Chicago to the end of the pier in Santa Monica.

properties.name: Historic Route 66 Begin Sign
properties.notes: The road starts on Adams Street across from the Art Institute, where a brown Begin sign marks mile zero. Westbound traffic leaves on Adams; the matching End sign is a block south on Jackson.
properties.address: E Adams St & S Michigan Ave, Chicago, IL 60603

properties.name: Lou Mitchell's
properties.notes: A diner since 1923, a few blocks from the start of the road. Big omelets, double-yolk eggs and a free donut hole while you wait in line.

properties.name: Dell Rhea's Chicken Basket
properties.notes: A roadhouse serving fried chicken on this stretch of old 66 since the 1940s, now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

properties.name: Launching Pad Drive-In
properties.notes: Home of the Gemini Giant, a fiberglass spaceman holding a rocket since the 1960s. The old drive-in building has been restored as a stop with food and Route 66 souvenirs.

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Polk-a-Dot Drive In
properties.notes: A 1950s burger stand with fiberglass statues of Elvis, Marilyn Monroe and the Blues Brothers out front. Order a malt and pose for the photo.

properties.name: Illinois Route 66 Hall of Fame & Museum
properties.notes: A free museum in Pontiac's old firehouse, with road artist Bob Waldmire's converted school bus and VW van parked out back. Look for the murals around the courthouse square.

properties.name: Funks Grove Pure Maple Sirup
properties.notes: A family that has tapped these maples since the 1800s and spells it sirup the old way. The shop keeps limited, seasonal hours, so check before you count on it.

properties.name: Cozy Dog Drive In
properties.notes: The family that claims the corn dog on a stick still runs this Springfield counter. The walls are covered with Route 66 memorabilia.

properties.name: Lincoln Home National Historic Site
properties.notes: The only house Abraham Lincoln ever owned, set in four restored blocks of his old neighborhood. Free ranger-led tours start at the visitor center.

properties.name: Ariston Cafe
properties.notes: A dining room in a 1935 brick building that has served travelers on the road since the 1920s. Good for a sit-down lunch between Springfield and St. Louis.

properties.name: Old Chain of Rocks Bridge
properties.notes: A mile-long former Route 66 bridge over the Mississippi, with a 22-degree bend in the middle, now open only to walkers and cyclists. Park on the Illinois side.
properties.address: Chain of Rocks Rd, Granite City, IL 62040

properties.name: Gateway Arch National Park
properties.notes: The 630-foot stainless steel arch on the riverfront, with a museum underneath and small tram pods to the top. Book tram times ahead on the official site.

properties.name: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard
properties.notes: A walk-up custard stand on Chippewa Street, an old 66 alignment, since 1941. Order a concrete, so thick it is handed over upside down. Closed for part of the winter.

properties.name: Meramec Caverns
properties.notes: The cave that painted its name on barn roofs all along the road. Guided tours walk through large lit chambers along the Meramec River.

properties.name: Wagon Wheel Motel
properties.notes: Stone cottages from the 1930s, restored with modern rooms and a working neon sign. Cuba's downtown murals are a short walk away.

properties.name: Missouri Hick Bar-B-Que
properties.notes: Barbecue smoked over hickory in a big log building next door to the Wagon Wheel. Easy dinner without moving the car.

properties.name: Devil's Elbow Bridge
properties.notes: A 1923 steel truss bridge over a tight bend of the Big Piney River on a bypassed loop of old 66. Pull off for the bluffs and the quiet.

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: 66 Drive-In Theatre
properties.notes: A 1949 drive-in movie screen still showing films on the old highway west of Carthage. It runs from spring to fall only; check the schedule.

properties.name: Cars on the Route
properties.notes: A restored 1930s Kan-O-Tex service station on Kansas's short stretch of 66. The rusty tow truck out front helped inspire Mater in Cars.

properties.name: Rainbow Bridge
properties.notes: The last surviving concrete Marsh arch bridge on Route 66, built in 1923 over Brush Creek. A newer road now runs alongside, so pull off and walk across for the photo.

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Coleman Theatre
properties.notes: A 1929 Spanish Revival vaudeville house on Main Street with its original theater organ. Volunteers lead tours on most days; check the theater's site.

properties.name: Blue Whale of Catoosa
properties.notes: A grinning 80-foot concrete whale built in the early 1970s as an anniversary gift, sitting in a spring-fed pond. A free photo stop.

properties.name: Cyrus Avery Route 66 Memorial Bridge and Centennial Plaza
properties.notes: A plaza at the old 11th Street bridge honoring Tulsa's Cyrus Avery, who helped create Route 66, with a large bronze of a family car meeting a horse-drawn wagon.

properties.name: The Campbell Hotel
properties.notes: A 1927 building on 11th Street, Tulsa's stretch of Route 66, restored as a boutique hotel with individually themed rooms.

properties.name: Tally's Good Food Cafe
properties.notes: A neon-lit diner on 11th Street with chicken-fried steak, cinnamon rolls the size of a plate and breakfast all day.

properties.name: Rock Cafe
properties.notes: A 1939 cafe built from sandstone dug up during road construction. Order a burger or the chicken-fried steak at the counter.

properties.name: Arcadia Round Barn
properties.notes: A big round red barn from 1898, restored by local volunteers, with a small museum downstairs and a dance loft upstairs.

properties.name: POP's 66
properties.notes: A modern gas station and diner under a 66-foot steel soda bottle that lights up at night. Inside, coolers hold hundreds of different sodas.

properties.name: Lucille's Service Station
properties.notes: A 1929 two-story gas station where Lucille Hamons sold gas and kindness to travelers for decades. Now preserved as a roadside stop on the old road.

properties.name: Oklahoma Route 66 Museum
properties.notes: A state-run museum with rooms that walk through the road decade by decade, from the Dust Bowl exodus to the neon motel era. Plan an hour or more.

properties.name: National Route 66 & Transportation Museum
properties.notes: A museum complex with a re-created old town, a farm and transportation museum, and a giant Route 66 sign for photos.

properties.name: U-Drop Inn
properties.notes: A 1936 Art Deco gas station and cafe, now the town visitor center. Come back after dark when the green and pink neon is on.

properties.name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
properties.notes: The home of the 72-ounce steak challenge, with a motel and brewery on the same lot. Loud and kitschy, and that is the point.
properties.address: 7701 Interstate 40 East Access Rd, Amarillo, TX 79118

properties.name: Cadillac Ranch
properties.notes: Ten Cadillacs buried nose-down in a field west of Amarillo by the Ant Farm art collective in 1974. Bring spray paint; everyone adds a layer.

properties.name: Route 66 Midpoint
properties.notes: A sign in tiny Adrian marks the halfway point: 1,139 miles to Chicago and 1,139 to Los Angeles.

properties.name: Blue Swallow Motel
properties.notes: A 1939 motor court with a garage beside each room and one of the best neon signs on the road. Book ahead in summer.

properties.name: Motel Safari
properties.notes: A 1959 motel restored with clean mid-century rooms and a camel on the sign. A good second choice if the Blue Swallow is full.

properties.name: Tee Pee Curios
properties.notes: A 1940s gift shop with a concrete tepee entrance and a neon sign that lights the street at night.

properties.name: Del's Restaurant
properties.notes: A family restaurant under a neon cow sign, serving New Mexican plates with red or green chile since 1956.

properties.name: Blue Hole
properties.notes: A clear, cold artesian spring about 80 feet deep, popular with scuba divers and for a bracing swim on a hot day.
properties.address: 1085 Blue Hole Rd, Santa Rosa, NM 88435

properties.name: Route 66 Auto Museum
properties.notes: Rows of hot rods, classic cars and road signs in a big shed on the east side of town.

properties.name: 66 Diner
properties.notes: A 1950s-style diner on Central Avenue, Albuquerque's long stretch of 66, with burgers, green chile and thick shakes.

properties.name: KiMo Theatre
properties.notes: A 1927 theater in the Pueblo Deco style, with painted ceilings and steer-skull light fixtures. The city runs shows and occasional tours.

properties.name: Richardson's Trading Company
properties.notes: A trading post in business since 1913, with rooms full of Navajo rugs, Zuni jewelry and pawn.

properties.name: El Rancho Hotel
properties.notes: A 1937 hotel built for movie crews shooting westerns nearby. Rooms are named for the stars who stayed, and signed photos line the lobby balcony.

properties.name: Petrified Forest National Park
properties.notes: The only national park that Route 66 crossed; an old Studebaker marks the alignment. Drive the park road from the Painted Desert to the log fields and exit to Holbrook.
properties.address: 1 Park Rd, Petrified Forest National Park, AZ 86028

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Wigwam Motel
properties.notes: Fifteen concrete tepees from 1950, each with a vintage car parked out front. Book directly with the motel.

properties.name: Standin' on the Corner Park
properties.notes: A street corner in Winslow made famous by the Eagles song, with a statue and a mural of a flatbed Ford.

properties.name: La Posada Hotel
properties.notes: Mary Colter's 1930 railroad hotel, rescued and restored with gardens and art-filled halls. Trains still roll past the back door.

properties.name: The Turquoise Room
properties.notes: The dining room at La Posada, cooking Southwestern food with local lamb and heirloom corn.

match.query: The Turquoise Room at La Posada

properties.name: Meteor Crater
properties.notes: A crater almost a mile wide left by an impact about 50,000 years ago. A visitor center and observation decks sit on the rim, six miles south of the interstate.

properties.name: Lowell Observatory
properties.notes: The observatory on Mars Hill where Pluto was found in 1930. Come at night for telescope viewing under Flagstaff's dark skies.
properties.address: 1400 W Mars Hill Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86001

properties.name: Hotel Monte Vista
properties.notes: A 1927 downtown hotel with a long list of movie-star guests and ghost stories. A block from the old 66 and the railroad.
properties.address: 100 N San Francisco St, Flagstaff, AZ 86001

properties.name: Grand Canyon Railway Depot
properties.notes: The 1908 depot where trains leave for the South Rim. Williams was the last Route 66 town bypassed by the interstate, and its main street still has the neon.
properties.address: 233 N Grand Canyon Blvd, Williams, AZ 86046

properties.name: Delgadillo's Snow Cap
properties.notes: A burger stand opened in 1953 by Juan Delgadillo, known for its pranks: fake mustard bottles and a menu of jokes. The family still runs it.

properties.name: Angel & Vilma Delgadillo's Original Route 66 Gift Shop
properties.notes: The former barbershop of Angel Delgadillo, who led the campaign to have the old road named a historic highway. Busy with souvenirs and stories.

properties.name: Hackberry General Store
properties.notes: A roadside store stacked with old gas pumps, signs and a red Corvette, on the long empty stretch between Peach Springs and Kingman.

properties.name: Arizona Route 66 Museum
properties.notes: A museum inside the 1907 Kingman powerhouse, covering the road from wagon trails to the motel era. The visitor center is in the same building.
properties.address: 120 W Andy Devine Ave, Kingman, AZ 86401

properties.name: Mr. D'z Route 66 Diner
properties.notes: A turquoise and pink diner across from the powerhouse, serving burgers, root beer and breakfast.
properties.address: 105 E Andy Devine Ave, Kingman, AZ 86401

properties.name: Oatman Hotel
properties.notes: A 1902 adobe in an old gold-mining town where wild burros wander the street. The bar walls are papered with signed dollar bills. Expect sharp switchbacks over Sitgreaves Pass to get here.

properties.name: Roy's Motel and Café
properties.notes: A 1959 boomerang sign in the Mojave, at a stop with a small store and gas. Parts of National Trails Highway close for repairs; check San Bernardino County road status.

properties.name: Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch
properties.notes: A field of welded metal trees hung with colored glass bottles, built by Elmer Long. Free to wander; stay on the paths.
properties.address: 24266 National Trails Hwy, Oro Grande, CA 92368

properties.name: California Route 66 Museum
properties.notes: A small volunteer-run museum on old 66 in Victorville with a VW hippie van, signs and road memorabilia.

properties.name: Wigwam Motel
properties.notes: The 1949 California sibling of the Holbrook motel: concrete tepees around a pool on Foothill Boulevard, the old 66.
properties.address: 2728 W Foothill Blvd, San Bernardino, CA 92410

properties.name: Fair Oaks Pharmacy
properties.notes: A 1915 drugstore with a restored soda fountain on the old route through South Pasadena. Phosphates, malts and egg creams at the counter.

properties.name: Barney's Beanery
properties.notes: A roadhouse on Santa Monica Boulevard, the last leg of Route 66, at this spot since 1927. Chili, pool tables and license plates on the ceiling.
properties.address: 8447 Santa Monica Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069

properties.name: Santa Monica Pier
properties.notes: The end of the road. The Route 66 End of the Trail sign stands on the pier, past the carousel; walk out for the ocean and the Ferris wheel.
properties.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
